_note: Every number here is measured or computed from a file in this repo. Do not add numbers that are not here. null = not measured yet.

effect.name: CF Muff
effect.models: 1974 'Violet Ram's Head' Big Muff Pi (circuit model by Comet Flower): asymmetric-rail Q1 booster, two diode + 560 pF feedback clip stages, exact tone network, recovery stage
effect.platform: Zoom G1X Four (TI C6745 DSP), stock effect format (.ZD2), 44.1 kHz

test_signal: 440 Hz sine from the Probe 10 diagnostic effect in slot 0, recorded dry through VPE at 44.1 kHz

pedal_measurements.source: recon/04_hardware_log.md, take VPB_2026-10-08_214128_dry.wav, analysed with tools/tone_harmonics.py method

cf_muff.reading: Odd harmonics dominate (symmetric clipping, as in a Big Muff). Aliasing (inharmonic content above 2 kHz) at the recording's noise floor even at -6 dB THD.

real_big_muff.status: pending: owner records a physical Big Muff with the same 440 Hz tone and settings

dsp_cost.source: recon/04, take VPB_2026-10-08_231435_dry.wav, CF MuffT cycle-counter diagnostic (tools/decode_memprobe.py), 2 frames agreeing to 0.01%
dsp_cost.note: Static code count matched the pedal for CF Muff, CF RAT (17.2k) and CF 808 (17.4k). The total per-block budget is still under investigation; do not state a percentage of the DSP.

declared_load.rule: Zoom's own effects declare 3.3-3.7 load units per 1,000 cycles/block (TS Drive 3.65, Gold Drive 3.41, Zen Drive 3.37, DS-1 3.33, NYC Muff 3.42, Squeak 3.69; recon/11). CF Muff = 3.7 x 14.14k = 53, the top of Zoom's range. Zoom's NYC Muff declares 34.86.
declared_load.why: The stock firmware sums declared loads and refuses an overloaded patch (PROCESS OVERFLOW). Declaring honestly keeps a patch from overrunning the DSP.

bench_accuracy.source: docs/helpers/MUFF_RESULT.md (host bench vs Comet Flower's reference circuit model)
bench_accuracy.tolerance: harmonics within 1.5 dB, aliasing below -50 dB

mobile_core_reference.label: Comet Flower's own mobile core, same bench

checks_passed: Fits its 40 KiB load slot with 23,936 bytes spare
Valid file CRC and standard DRIVE effect header
Effect file only: does not modify the pedal firmware
Runs on the G1X Four: played and timed 2026-10-08
pending: Overflow-guard test: with heavy stock effects the pedal must show PROCESS OVERFLOW, not freeze
Install test on an unmodified stock firmware (our pedal's firmware differs from stock only in the start-up logo and text)
safety.install_note: Install through update-mode images where possible; an interrupted USB file transfer bricked our test pedal once (recovered, docs/RECOVERY_G1.md).

published_reference.source: ElectroSmash, 'Big Muff Pi Analysis' (www.electrosmash.com/big-muff-pi-analysis): 1976-77 'V3' red/black Big Muff, circuit analysis
published_reference.cf_muff_source: CF Muff tone tables (effects/muffx/blob.bin, MUFF_TONE), biquad response computed at 176.4 kHz, Tone at noon
published_reference.caveat: Different version: CF Muff models the 1974 Ram's Head, ElectroSmash analyses the 1976-77 V3. Stage gains are not compared: CF Muff's input-booster gain (16.7 dB) and filter corners (94 Hz, 1.2 kHz) were taken from the same article, so comparing them would be circular.
